#3194 · never block a user-typed invocation

Two defects in one class: you typed a command and the system refused it.

Defect 1 — our flag blocked your words

① fresh prompt          harness EXPANDS /ork:brainstorm itself
                        → Skill tool never called
                        → flag never consulted        ✅ runs

② mid-turn steering     harness does NOT expand it
                        → model must call the Skill tool
                        → disable-model-invocation: true denies it   ❌ refused

The flag was meant to say "model, don't pick this on your own." It also said "model, ignore the user." CC honored exactly what we declared — this was ours, not upstream. All 10 user-invocable skills carrying it flipped to false.

⚠ New risk the flip introduces, and the guard added for it

Model-invocable also means the model may auto-select these. Two descriptions matched routine work done dozens of times per session:

commit     "Use when committing changes..."      ← 23 manual git commits this session
create-pr  "Use when opening PRs..."             ← 11 manual gh pr create

both now lead with: "Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks for this
skill; routine git work must stay a direct command."

implement, swarm-migrate, ci-sentinel and setup already carried adequate negative guards ("Not for fixing a bug…", "Do NOT use for single-repo work").

Defect 2 — yesterday's fix never reached the layer that reads it

src/skills/*/SKILL.md          background: false   23 skills ✅
        │
        ▼  generate_command_from_skill()
   PASSTHROUGH_KEYS = (disable-model-invocation model effort
                       context agent user-invocable name)
                       ↑ background absent → silently dropped
        │
        ▼
plugins/ork/commands/*.md      background:         0 / 35 files ❌

#3239 shipped the opt-out to the skill layer, but the slash-command path reads the generated command file — so the fix was inert exactly where it was aimed. Third instance of this drop, after argument-hint (#3146) and disable-model-invocation. Now 23/35 command files carry it, and the passthrough gate classifies the key so it can never be dropped silently again.

The bill — paid deliberately, not hidden

budgetbeforeafternew cap
skill index (bytes)224662701627300
session total (tokens)90791021610400

Both ratchets carry a comment naming #3194 as the purchase and repeating the standing rule: ratchet DOWN as trimming lands, never raise to clear a regression.

Why 7 of the 10 were never typed — the revealed preference

quickviz        71  ┐
assess          34  │ COGNITION — delegated
brainstorm      18  │ (thinking, seeing, judging)
visualize-plan  11  │
verify          11  ┘
─────────────────────────────────────────────
commit · create-pr · implement · setup       ┐ MECHANICS — never delegated
swarm-migrate · ci-sentinel · audit-activation ┘ (0 typed uses, all time)

Not a discoverability failure. Mechanics are already one command away and the hook layer enforces what those skills would add — the commit-nudge hook suggested /ork:commit 9 times in a single session and was ignored every time. ci-sentinel is the real miss, but it wants a cron deployment, not a keystroke.
